cohort: The study participants were women experiencing primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) due to uterine atony following lower segment cesarean section (LSCS).
finding: Both Bilateral Uterine Artery Ligation (BUAL) and B-Lynch sutures demonstrate comparable efficacy and safety in managing primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) due to uterine atony following lower segment cesarean section (LSCS).
mod_finding: Subgroup analyses based on the mode of delivery showed no significant differences in intraoperative blood loss between the BUAL and B-Lynch suture groups.
